Vultures are constantly struggling for the survival of the species which suggests Darwin’s theory “Struggle for Existence”. Darwin noticed that, in three phases this struggle is done in life. They are-
(i) Interspecific Struggle: For example, a frog eats an insect and a snake eats a frog. A peacock eats both snake and frog. Thus only due to physical needs (hunger), a cruel relationship develops among different species, where each species plays the role of food or consumer.
(ii) Intraspecific Stuggle: As the same species has the same habitat and the same food habits, when their number increases, they compete among themselves for survival. For example, when in an island the number of herbivorous animal increases, they fight for food and shelter among themselves. The stronger animal (herbivorous) beat the weaker ones and take the comand of that area. As a result, the weaker animals die after a certain period from starvation.
(iii) Struggle with Environment: Normal life of living organisms is interrupted by unfavourable conditions like flood, drought, cyclone and tornado, earthquake, volcano eruption etc. So living beings always have to fight with these unfavourable environment to survive. Those who won the struggle can survive, while other become extinct. This is a general truth in the series of evolution.
In reality, sometimes the amount of chromosomes increases and new species are developed.
All the organisms of the world going through sexual reproduction have some differences which indicates differences in genes. The change in genes after sexual reproduction causes varities in genes. The continuous changes in the genes at one stage causes the creation of a new species. If the variety is suitable for the environment then for it will help the organism to survive. The survival of a species depends on the amount of variety among its member organisms. The environment is continuously changing. Those species survive which atleast have some members who can adapt to the changing environment. If any species of animals have less varieties then the possibility of surviving in the changing environment decreases. As a result, the entire species can become extinct. When the amount of variety among the members are more in a species the changing environment can still keep some of the members alive.
Hence, the process in Scenario-2, can create varieties in gene and can also create a new species due to continuous changes.

Parents : Tall (Tt) × Short (Tt)
Gamete : T t T t

Color blindness is a hereditary disease. There are some pigments in the optical nerves of humans to properly identify colors. Color blindness is caused due to the deficiency of color-identifying pigments in the optical nerves. The pigments are controlled by two genes and the genes are situated in the X chromosome which are passed down to the offspring in sexual reproduction. If the genes for identifying pigment are absent in the X chromosome of parents, then they are also found to be absent in the offspring. If only one pigment is absent, the person cannot differentiate between red and green. Again, if more than one pigment is absent, then the person also cannot differentiate between blue and yellow.
On the other hand, thalassemia is a disease of the abnormal state of the blood. Red blood corpuscles are made of two types of proteins, namely α-globulin and β-globulin. Thalassemia is caused due to defects in the genes of these proteins. If the baby gets the thalassemia gene from either of the parents, it does not show any symptoms of thalassemia. If the baby obtains the genes from both the parents, it suffers from severe anemia just from the first year of birth. In case of severe thalassemia, the baby dies in the mother’s womb. Besides, if the patients with thalassemia show the symptoms of jaundice, diabetes etc., they do not get to live more than 30 years.
